overview: This paper introduces M3IRT and M2IRT, multimodal and multidimensional item response theory frameworks that decompose model ability and question difficulty into modality-specific and cross-modal components to evaluate cross-modal reasoning in MLLMs, filter low-quality shortcut questions, and construct compact, high-quality benchmark subsets via Computer Adaptive Testing.

modules.name: Dataset Preparation & Low-Quality Question Synthesis
modules.description: Load and preprocess multimodal benchmarks (MMMU, MATHVISTA, SEED-BENCH), and implement the semi-synthetic data generation pipeline that swaps image/text inputs to create artificial shortcut or unsolvable questions for robustness evaluation.

modules.name: Response Matrix & Tensor Construction
modules.description: Construct the 2D response matrix for standard models and the 3D response tensor for M2IRT/M3IRT, encoding the success/failure records of VLMs across questions under different modality input formats (image-only, text-only, image+text, none).

modules.name: M2IRT Model Implementation
modules.description: Implement the Multimodal Item Response Theory (M2IRT) model, defining modality-decomposed scalar parameters for subject ability, item difficulty, and item discrimination, along with the forward pass calculating response probabilities based on input format indicators.

modules.name: M3IRT Model Implementation
modules.description: Implement the Multimodal Multidimensional Item Response Theory (M3IRT) model, extending M2IRT into a vectorized formulation with diagonal format indicator matrices, computing response probabilities via the interaction of modality-decomposed parameter vectors.

modules.name: M2IRT & M3IRT Training Pipeline
modules.description: Implement the negative log-likelihood loss function and the stochastic gradient descent training loop with Adam optimizer, supporting partially observed response tensors and hyperparameter search for the parameter upper bound.

modules.name: Fisher Information & D-Optimality Computation
modules.description: Calculate the Fisher Information scalar for M2IRT and the Fisher Information matrix for M3IRT, and implement the D-optimality criterion to minimize estimation uncertainty for adaptive item selection.

modules.name: Computer Adaptive Testing (CAT) Module
modules.description: Implement the CAT algorithm that iteratively selects the most informative questions from an item pool based on Fisher Information or D-optimality, updates the subject's ability estimation, and generates compact benchmark subsets.

modules.name: Baseline Methods Implementation
modules.description: Implement or integrate baseline evaluation and subset selection methods including Random sampling, standard IRT, standard MIRT, TinyBenchmarks, and FlashEval, adapting them to the multimodal benchmark context.

modules.name: Subset Extraction & Model Ranking Evaluation
modules.description: Extract subsets of varying sizes using CAT and baselines, estimate VLM performance on these subsets, compute model rankings, and evaluate ranking fidelity against the original full-benchmark ranking using Spearman's rank correlation.

modules.name: Low-Quality Question Contamination Analysis
modules.description: Calculate the proportion of artificially generated low-quality questions in the extracted subsets, and evaluate the robustness of M2IRT/M3IRT in filtering out shortcuts compared to baseline methods under different contamination rates.

modules.name: Missing Response Prediction & AUC Evaluation
modules.description: Evaluate the models as latent variable methods by predicting missing responses from observed ones, splitting data into train/val/test sets, and computing the ROC-AUC score to assess prediction accuracy on noisy benchmarks.

modules.name: Parameter Interpretation & Visualization
modules.description: Extract and visualize the decomposed latent parameters (base, image, text, cross-modal abilities and difficulties), generate plots for ability distributions across VLMs, and qualitatively analyze examples of high and low cross-modal difficulty questions.

modules.name: Statistical Significance Testing
modules.description: Implement statistical tests such as the Wilcoxon signed-rank test to compare the performance of the proposed methods against baselines, and the Mann-Whitney U test to verify significant differences between original and low-quality question parameter distributions.
